newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian dam's IPO seen drawing good interest.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian dam's IPO seen drawing good interest.

text.p: The initial public offering (IPO) of Malaysia's Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp, the holding firm of the $5.5 billion Bakun dam, has attracted good interest from local and foreign investors, the IPO's adviser said on Monday.

Asked about the response to the IPO, involving 1.5 billion shares at two ringgit a share, Tan Choon Thye, head of corporate finance at Commerce International Merchant Bankers Bhd said, said, "So far, still so good."
He said in an interview with Reuters that the IPO includes foreign investors, who along with large Malaysian institutions are expected to take up 10 percent of Bakun Hydro-Electric's capital.
Bakun will also sell 15 percent of its shares to the Malaysian public.
The Asian Wall Street Journal on Monday said Ekran Bhd, the main contractor of the dam, was considering scrapping a plan to offer shares in the project to foreign investors due to lukewarm response.
Tan denied this, saying that Ekran officials have said there was a good response from foreign investors.
Ekran officials could not be reached for comment on Monday.

The size of the offering has raised fears that the market would face a liquidity drain when the stock lists. But Ekran executive chairman Ting Pek Khing has said the IPO would not destabilise the market and that the offering would take just 750 million ringgit from the public out of a total flotation of 3.0 billion ringgit.
The other 2.25 billion ringgit would be held by the major shareholders in the dam: Ekran, the Sarawak government, state electricity firm Tenaga Nasional and other government entities.

The Bakun dam is under construction in a Sarawak rainforest on Borneo island. The dam would create a reservoir the size of Singapore and clear 69,000 hectares (170,499 acres) of forest. It is scheduled for completion by 2003.

The stock is expected to list in June, and Tan said the deal participants are "trying to tidy up the timing" of the IPO and its road show. He said the listing should "still be around that time", but was unable to be more specific.
Prospectuses for the offering have not been yet issued, he said.
The project has been criticised by environmentalists and tribals displaced by the construction. But with Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad as its chief supporter, it has gone ahead.
Market talk has suggested the offering would not be well received because of the controversy and the uncertainty of the investment returns.
Asked about scepticism toward the IPO, Tan said: "We are confident."
